stem: A spherical drop of radius $R$ is divided into eight equal droplets. If surface tension is $T$, then the work done in this process is
solution:
Volume of 8 small droplets = Volume of 1 big drop

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\times8 = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{R}{2}$

Work done = (Change in area) $\times$ surface tension

$$= (4\pi r^2\times8 - 4\pi R^2)T = \left(4\pi\frac{R^2}{4}\times8 - 4\pi R^2\right)T = 4\pi R^2T$$

stem: A round disc of moment of inertia $I_2$ about its axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through its centre is placed over another disc of moment of inertia $I_1$ rotating with an angular velocity $\omega$ about the same axis. The final angular velocity of the combination of discs is
solution:
According to conservation of angular momentum

$I_1\omega = (I_1 + I_2)\omega_2 \Rightarrow \omega_2 = \dfrac{I_1\omega}{I_1 + I_2}$

Three particles, each of mass $m$ grams are situated at the vertices of an equilateral triangle $ABC$ of side $l$ cm (as shown in the figure). The moment of inertia of the system about a line $AX$ perpendicular to $AB$ and in the plane of $ABC$ in g-cm$^2$ units will be:
solution:
Moment of inertia of the system about AX: $m_Ar_A^2 + m_Br_B^2 + m_Cr_C^2$

where $r_A = 0$, $r_B = l$, $r_C = l\sin30^\circ$

$$m(0)^2 + m(l)^2 + m(l\sin30^\circ)^2 = ml^2 + \frac{ml^2}{4} = \frac{5}{4}ml^2$$

Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) value can be a measure of water pollution caused by the organic matter. Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Polluted water has BOD value higher than 10 ppm
Aerobic bacteria decreases the BOD value
Anaerobic bacteria increases the BOD value
Clean water has BOD value higher than 10 ppm
solution: Clean water has BOD less than 5 ppm, whereas highly polluted water has BOD value of 17 ppm or more. Thus polluted water has BOD higher than 10 ppm.

stem:
In the reaction:

$\text{CH}_3-\underset{\text{CH}_3}{\text{CH}}-\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3 + \text{HI} \xrightarrow{\text{Heated}}$

Which of the following compounds will be formed?
solution:
The ether is protonated by $\text{H}^+$; cleavage gives the $1^\circ$ carbocation $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H}_2$ and $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

The $1^\circ$ carbocation rearranges (hydride/methyl shift) to the $2^\circ$ carbocation $\text{CH}_3\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{HCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which combines with $\text{I}^-$ to give $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(I)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.
Nitrobenzene (A) $\xrightarrow{\text{Sn + HCl}}$ Aniline (B) $\xrightarrow{\text{CHCl}_3 + \text{KOH}}$ Phenyl isocyanide (C) $\xrightarrow{\text{Na/C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}}$ N-methylaniline

stem: The correct stability order of following species is -
solution:
x is a conjugated, highly substituted diene (most stable, resonance + hyperconjugation); w is a less stabilised (non-conjugated/less substituted) diene; z is a cumulated diene (allene), less stable; y is cyclobutadiene, which is antiaromatic and least stable.

Hence $x > w > z > y$.

options: The S-S-S bond angles in the $\text{S}_8$ and $\text{S}_6$ rings are the same.
Rhombic and monoclinic sulphur have $\text{S}_8$ molecules
solution: The $\text{S}_6$ molecule has a chair-form hexagon ring with approximately the same bond length as that in $\text{S}_8$ (205.7 pm vs 204 pm), but with somewhat smaller bond angles ($102.2^\circ$ vs $107^\circ$), i.e. bond lengths are approximately same but angles are different.
